newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia presidency to meet soon - Serb, Croat leaders.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia presidency to meet soon - Serb, Croat leaders.

text.p: Bosnia's Serb and Croat leaders, both members of the Bosnia's three-man presidency, ended two days of talks on Thursday in Pale and said a crisis over power-sharing would be resolved soon.

"Yesterday and today Mr (Kresimir) Zubak and I met to discuss the constitution of joint bodies and ways of overcoming the present difficult situation, the small crisis," Bosnian Serb leader Momcilo Krajisnik told reporters.
"We both concluded that utmost must be done to resolve the situation and...we share great optimism this will be achieved," he said.
The three-man presidency, like other joint governing bodies of the post-Dayton accord Bosnia, have yet to function properly since a general election last month.

The Serbs have shied away from the inagural session of the presidency and a joint parliament two weeks ago, claiming security fears. They also refused to sign an oath of loyalty to the Bosnian constitution.
The rotating presidency comprises Zubak, Krajisnik and Moslem leader Alija Izetbegovic.
Zubak, who was in telephone contact with Izetbegovic and was rewarded for his efforts by being described by Krajisnik as "a Moslem-Croat (Henry) Kissinger", shared Krajisnik's optimism:
"I can only reiterate Mr Krajisnik's views. I think we are on a good road to overcome the situation we are in now."
Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prljic announced in Sarajevo on Wednesday that the next meeting of the presidency would be held next week.
